problem: Given a curve $x=y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)?$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y\sqrt{y}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2})-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2y+2 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(8,4),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(8,4)} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{4}-4+2)}=1.\end{aligned}
$$
